Current ideation absent; intent absent; plan absent; access reviewed true. Disposition: No suicidal ideation, intent, plan or past suicide attempt. He expects that he may be killed and has accepted the risk, which is a realistic appraisal, not a wish to die. Risk factors weighed: an impulsive act of self-injury in grief at twelve, an anonymous letter urging him to end his life, depression, insomnia and isolation of leadership. Outpatient care with a safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number, and review at every visit.

text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Psychiatry consultation in two weeks to confirm the diagnosis, assess for PTSD and safety, and advise on therapy and medicine
  • Assessment at intake: blood count, metabolic panel, TSH, lipids, hemoglobin A1c and ECG; PHQ-9, GAD-7, PC-PTSD-5 and AUDIT-C; Insomnia Severity Index and sleep apnea screening; safety plan with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number
  • Tobacco: advice to quit, an offer of counseling and medicine, and a quit plan agreed by shared decision
  • Blood pressure: validated home monitoring, twice morning and evening for seven days, before a diagnosis is made
  • Privacy: a restricted chart with audited access, documentation kept to what care requires, and a choice of therapist, including a Black clinician if he prefers
  • Depression and insomnia: weekly cognitive behavioral therapy with CBT for insomnia (fixed rising time, a sleep window, no work in bed), respecting his faith; sertraline 25 mg daily for a week, then 50 mg, by shared decision; no hypnotic
  • A sustainable work plan: one full day a week without work, no more than two speeches a day, delegation of travel and correspondence, and a two-week break in the summer
  • Varenicline 0.5 mg daily for three days, twice daily for four days, then 1 mg twice daily for twelve weeks, with a quit date on day eight and weekly telephone counseling; mood and sleep watched
  • Stage 1 hypertension at low estimated risk: lifestyle treatment (sodium below 1,500 to 2,300 mg a day, DASH-style eating, 150 minutes of activity a week, weight loss, no tobacco), home readings, urine albumin and a fundus examination; medicine if home readings stay at or above 130/80 after three to six months

resource.title: Martin Luther King Jr. synthetic care plan
resource.description: Caring for a 36-year-old Black minister and public leader with exhaustion, insomnia and low mood under sustained, real threat: distinguishing major depressive disorder from an adjustment disorder by DSM-5-TR, and realistic vigilance from PTSD (PC-PTSD-5 and interview); a structured safety assessment that separates the expectation of being killed from suicidal ideation and weighs a childhood act of self-injury and a letter urging suicide; CBT, CBT for insomnia and sertraline by shared decision under the APA 1958 guideline and the ACP insomnia guideline; tobacco cessation with counseling and varenicline under the USPSTF 1960 recommendation and the EAGLES trial; confirming stage 1 hypertension with home readings and lifestyle treatment under the 1956 ACC/AHA guideline; lipids and risk at 36; an old thoracotomy scar; a sustainable work plan; and equity in care: racism and threat as causes of stress, trust and privacy for a patient under surveillance, and culturally responsive therapy that respects his faith.
